review_candidates.description: Job Description Programme Analyst, GBV/IMS The Position The Programme Analyst: GBV/IMS plays a critical role in strengthening the quality, accessibility, and utility of data related to Gender-Based Violence (GBV) programming within the UNFPA Country Office. S/he is the technical focal point for the effective operation, management, and security of the GBV Information Management System (IMS) and is responsible for ensuring that GBV programme data is collected, analysed, and reported in a timely, ethical, and safe manner. In a challenging operating environment like South Sudan, accurate, timely, and safe data is essential for effective programming, resource allocation, and accountability in the critical area of GBV response and prevention. The Programme Analyst will make a vital contribution by ensuring data integrity and its strategic use to inform life-saving interventions for women and girls. Under the direct supervision of the M&E Specialist, the Programme Analyst: GBV/IMS will be responsible for managing the GBV data stream within the Country Office. This includes overseeing the technical and operational aspects of the GBV IMS, supporting partners on data collection protocols, analysing GBV programme results for monitoring reports, and ensuring that all data activities comply with the highest ethical and safety standards for working with sensitive survivor data. How You Can Make a Difference The UNFPA Strategic Plan 2026–2029 serves as the organization’s final push to achieve the 2030 Agenda, centering its mission on four primary outcomes. It continues to prioritize the "three transformative results"—ending the unmet need for family planning, eliminating preventable maternal deaths, and stopping gender-based violence and harmful practices. A pivotal addition to this cycle is a fourth outcome focused on demographic resilience, which seeks to help nations navigate complex population shifts, such as aging and urbanization, while ensuring that individual rights and reproductive choices remain at the heart of national policies. To accelerate progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the plan shifts toward a more integrated approach that bridges humanitarian, development, and peace efforts. By leveraging advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence, UNFPA aims to pinpoint and support those "furthest behind," directly contributing to SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality). This strategic framework emphasizes sustainable financing and localized agility, ensuring that even in climate-vulnerable or conflict-affected regions, the global community remains on track to fulfill the promise of the 2030 goals Job Purpose The Programme Analyst, GBV/IMS, plays a crucial and strategic role within the challenging operational environment of South Sudan, where the integrity, timeliness, and ethical management of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) data are vital for effective humanitarian response. This function is essential for translating sensitive raw information into strategic intelligence, thereby ensuring that life-saving interventions for vulnerable women and girls are evidence-based, targeted, and maximally effective. The role serves as a pivotal contributor to informed decision-making and maintaining accountability within the critical sector of GBV response and prevention. Under the direct supervision of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist, the Programme Analyst acts as the central focal point for the entire GBV data stream within the Country Office, covering a comprehensive set of technical, operational, and coordination tasks. A core responsibility is assuming full technical and operational oversight of the GBV Information Management System (IMS), ensuring its architecture is robust, secure, and compliant with global standards, including necessary system maintenance, troubleshooting, and coordinating upgrades. Furthermore, the Analyst is responsible for capacity development by providing high-quality technical support to implementing partners and field teams. This involves designing and enforcing strict data collection protocols, tools, and methodologies, as well as conducting regular training on ethical data collection, informed consent, and accurate entry into the IMS to ensure consistency and accuracy across all operational areas. A crucial function involves the analysis of GBV programme results through the routine generation of analytical reports, dashboards, and programmatic summaries for internal monitoring, donor reporting, and external coordination mechanisms. This requires interpreting complex quantitative and qualitative data to identify trends, geographical hotspots, service gaps, and programmatic impact, thus informing adaptive management and evidence-based advocacy. Given the highly sensitive nature of survivor data, the Analyst is the guardian of ethical standards, rigorously ensuring all data activities comply with the highest international ethical and safety guidelines (e.g., "Do No Harm" and the GBVIMS Guiding Principles), including strict adherence to data protection, confidentiality protocols, and disaggregation practices. Finally, the Analyst facilitates inter-agency coordination by actively representing the Country Office in relevant data and information management working groups, contributing to standardizing data systems and ensuring aggregated, anonymized data is shared to foster a comprehensive, sector-wide understanding of the GBV situation and response in South Sudan. Responsibilities The Programme Analyst will be responsible for: GBV Information Management System (IMS) Management and Oversight Serve as the Country Office technical expert and administrator for the GBV IMS (e.g., Primero/GBVIMS+), including user management, system maintenance, and troubleshooting. Ensure strict adherence to the global GBVIMS/GBVIMS+ principles, including the Core Principles of Safety, Ethics, Confidentiality, and Do No Harm, throughout the data collection, storage, analysis, and sharing process. Lead the routine collection, compilation, cleaning, and processing of GBV programme data and case management statistics received from implementing partners. Design and maintain data dashboards, visualizations, and maps to present key GBV trends and programme achievements for management and reporting. Monitoring, Reporting, and Data Quality Assurance Support the M&E Specialist and the GBV Programme team in monitoring the progress of GBV interventions against key performance indicators (KPIs) outlined in the Annual Work Plans (AWPs) and Country Programme Document (CPD). The role focuses on substation physical layout design, primary equipment arrangement, busbar configuration, clearance management, and the integration of primary equipment within the overall substation design. The position works with PRIMTECH and/or Revit as primary design tools and coordinates closely with civil and structural engineering partners for foundations, buildings, and access requirements. The Primary Design Engineer ensures that primary designs are technically sound, constructable, and aligned with client requirements, grid connection specifications, and applicable standards. The role also supports equipment interface design between HV/MV primary equipment and the secondary, protection, and automation systems. Note: DCS Norway operates a competence-based resource model. While this job description defines the primary function of the role, individuals are expected to contribute across other engineering and project functions based on their competencies and the needs of the business. This approach supports team flexibility, professional development, and efficient resource utilisation across projects. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AIS Substation Design Develop physical layout designs for AIS high-voltage substations. Design busbar configurations, equipment spacing, and clearance management. Prepare primary equipment arrangement drawings and general arrangement plans. Ensure compliance with insulation coordination requirements and safety clearances. Coordinate with civil and structural engineering partners for foundations, structures, and buildings. Support constructability reviews and site-specific design considerations. GIS Substation Design Develop bay arrangement and layout designs for GIS substations. Design interfaces between GIS equipment and external connections (cable sealing ends, bushings, transformer interfaces). Support GIS extension philosophy and future expandability design. Ensure GIS layout integration with overall substation design. Coordinate with GIS equipment suppliers on layout requirements and interface details. MV Distribution Design Support MV distribution layout design for data center applications. Ensure MV distribution topology meets data center redundancy requirements (N+1, 2N, concurrent maintainability). Design MV switchgear room layouts and equipment arrangements. Coordinate MV design with data center MEP boundary requirements. Primary Equipment Integration Coordinate primary equipment interfaces with secondary, protection, and SCADA systems. Support specification of primary equipment (transformers, switchgear, busbars, cable systems). Ensure primary design is consistent with power system study results and equipment sizing. Prepare technical specifications for primary equipment procurement. Support equipment selection in coordination with the Procurement Engineer. Engineering Coordination & Documentation Coordinate primary design with all engineering disciplines and external engineering partners. Prepare and maintain primary design documentation, including layout drawings, sections, and elevations. Participate in engineering design reviews. Support preparation of as-built documentation. Ensure primary design documentation is complete for construction handover. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & COMPETENCIES Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering. Experience Minimum 5 years of experience in primary substation design. Experience with AIS and/or GIS substation layout design. Experience with HV equipment arrangement and clearance management. Experience coordinating with civil and structural disciplines. Experience in data center or industrial electrical infrastructure is a plus. Technical Skills Proficiency in PRIMTECH and/or Revit for primary substation design. Proficiency in AutoCAD for engineering drawings. Understanding of HV and MV primary equipment (transformers, switchgear, busbars). Knowledge of insulation coordination and safety clearance requirements. Working knowledge of ETAP for equipment sizing validation. Understanding of data center MV distribution and redundancy architectures. Knowledge of IEC standards for substation design. Familiarity with AIS and GIS substation configurations. Interpersonal & Communication Skills Excellent verbal and written communication in English (Portuguese is considered a plus). EU citizenship preferred to facilitate site visits across Scandinavia. Based in Lisbon or Porto, Portugal. Strong organisational and multitasking capabilities. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Ability to coordinate across multiple engineering disciplines. STRATEGIC PERFORMANCE METRICS (KPIs) Quality and accuracy of primary substation layout designs. Compliance with engineering standards, clearance requirements, and project specifications. Timely delivery of primary design documentation. Effective coordination with engineering disciplines and external partners. Constructability and feasibility of primary design solutions. HEALTH, SAFETY & ENVIRONMENT (HSE) Comply with all applicable health, safety, and environmental legislation, regulations, and company procedures. Integrate safety-by-design principles into all engineering and project activities, ensuring that designs and solutions prioritise the safety of personnel, equipment, and the environment. Participate in risk assessments and hazard identification activities relevant to the role. Report safety concerns, incidents, and near-misses in accordance with company HSE procedures. Support the development and maintenance of a positive safety culture within the team and across projects. Ensure compliance with the company Integrated Management System (IMS) covering quality, safety, and environmental standards. REPLACEMENT POLICY In case of absence of less than one month, the role will be supported by a Senior Engineer or the Head of Design. For absences exceeding one month, a temporary replacement will be appointed by senior management according to DCS Norway replacement policy guidelines. The replacement person will assume the key responsibilities outlined in this job description to ensure continuity of primary design engineering activities. BENEFITS Addition of variable performance based 0-10% (annual) bonus. This will depend on company and personal performance, and is further subject to an annual performance review; A meal allowance of €10,46 per working day, provided via meal card; Private health insurance coverage for the employee; 22 working days of annual leave, in accordance with Portuguese Labour Law; When you are out of Portugal for work, we will offer the nominal Portugal allowance (approximately €89 per day with 50% payment for last travel day), but the company will pay the accommodation and travel costs (which will be reflected in the contract). When you are away and are paid the daily living away allowance, the meal card payment is not payable.
